pairs.why: Both saucers are built the same way, and B's calmer silver body with a softer finish sits closer to the soft, toy-like real cards than A's darker, glossier teal.
B's rounded, three-dimensional saucer with a coloured underside reads instantly and has the chunky toy volume of the real cards, while A is a flat, plain disc.
B is a clean, recognisable astronaut helmet with smooth, toy-like rendering like the real cards, while A's blue-and-orange striped ball looks like an odd, made-up object.
B is built like a real helmet with a compact, readable silhouette, while A is a featureless white sphere on a sterile grey surface.
A's chunky telescope with warm brass and wood, set on a wooden floor, matches the bright, chunky props in the real cards better than B's thinner, dark navy tube.
B has the soft, painted, slightly textured cartoon finish and violet night sky of the real scenes, while A looks like a flat, dull grey 3D render.
B's warm-lit dome with a yellow door and steps has the inviting glow of the real cards' lit buildings, while A is cooler and more sterile.
The two drawings are almost identical in colour, finish and build, so neither is meaningfully closer to the real cards.
